sections.title: How the repertoire fits together
paras: This repertoire gives Black one set of answers to everything White is likely to play. Against 1.e4 Black plays 1...e5; against 1.d4, 1...d5 and ...e6; against 1.c4, 1...e5; against 1.Nf3, 1...d5.

The lines connect through shared structures. The open games after 1.e4 e5 teach quick development and central breaks with ...d5. The queen’s-pawn lines teach how to free the c8-bishop from behind a solid pawn chain. Many flank openings transpose into one of these two families, so the same plans keep coming back.
Use the explorer to read each line with its notes, then switch to Drill mode, where the trainer plays White’s moves and you play Black’s. Lines you get wrong come back in your review queue.
sections.key: Read each line in the explorer, then drill it until you can play your side without help.

sections.title: Against 1.e4
paras: Against 1.e4 the repertoire answers 1...e5 and aims for open, classical positions. Black develops quickly, castles, and fights for the centre with ...d6, ...d5 or ...c5 depending on how White sets up.

tree.note: White takes the centre and opens diagonals for the queen and the f1-bishop.

sections.title: Against 1.d4
paras: Against 1.d4 the repertoire holds the centre with 1...d5 and ...e6. The structure is solid, and Black’s main task is to free the c8-bishop, usually with ...b6 and ...Bb7 or by opening the position with ...c5 or ...dxc4.

sections.title: Typical middlegame plans
paras: Freeing the c8-bishop. In the queen’s-pawn lines, Black’s light-squared bishop is shut in by the pawns on e6 and d5. The three standard solutions are ...b6 and ...Bb7, the ...c5 break that opens the position, and ...dxc4 followed by ...b5 and ...Bb7. Know which one each line uses.

The ...d5 break in open games. After 1.e4 e5, Black often equalizes with ...d5 before White can consolidate the centre. The break works when Black’s pieces are ready to use the lines it opens, so time it after development, as in the Italian line with 8...d5.

Playing against an isolated pawn. Several lines leave White with an isolated d-pawn. Blockade the square in front of it with a knight, trade minor pieces to reduce White’s attacking chances, and bring rooks to the d-file to press the pawn in the endgame.

Queenside space against the Spanish bishop. In the lines with Bb5, the plan ...a6, ...b5, ...Na5 and ...c5 gains queenside space, removes the pressure on e5 and often trades off White’s strongest bishop.
sections.key: Every line has a plan: know which structure you are aiming for.

sections.title: Drill: every line
paras: The trainer plays your opponent’s moves, choosing among the branches of the repertoire, and you play your side. When you leave the repertoire, the trainer shows the move and its explanation, and the line goes into your review queue.
